newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam Hussein's son Uday shot and wounded, TV.
newsitem.headline: Saddam Hussein's son Uday shot and wounded, TV.

text.p: The eldest son of President Saddam Hussein, Uday, was shot and wounded on Thursday while driving in Baghdad, Iraq television reported.

"An official spokesman for the presidential office announced that Mr Uday Saddam Hussein, chairman of the Iraqi Olympic Committee, was subjected tonight to a cowardly attack during which he was wounded at 7 PM (1600 GMT)," the TV said.
The spokesman said Uday was driving in his personal car in the smart district of al-Mansour when the attack took place
He said Uday's condition "was not a matter of concern" and he was at the Ibn Sina hospital in Baghdad.
The spokesman said on Iraq TV that investigation into "this vicious crime" was underway.
This is the first reported attack on the life of Uday, aged 32, who runs Iraq's most influential newspaper, Babel, and a TV station.
President Saddam Hussein has two sons and three daughters.
Central Baghdad was quiet after the reported shooting.
